bottom_line: In patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban reduced the primary composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96).
implications: These data support that, compared with placebo, rivaroxaban reduced the composite end point (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96; P = 0.008) but increased major bleeding not related to CABG (2.1% vs. 0.6%, P<0.001) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.009); they do not support a significant difference in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66).

major_points.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial in 15,526 patients with recent acute coronary syndrome testing rivaroxaban 2.5 mg or 5 mg twice daily versus placebo.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 15,526 patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome to receive twice-daily doses of either 2.5 mg or 5 mg of rivaroxaban or placebo

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

major_points.text: Rivaroxaban reduced the primary efficacy end point versus placebo (8.9% vs. 10.7%; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.74–0.96; P=0.008).
major_points.quote: Rivaroxaban significantly reduced the primary efficacy end point, as compared with placebo, with respective rates of 8.9% and 10.7% (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.96; P = 0.008)

major_points.text: Both rivaroxaban doses reduced the primary efficacy end point versus placebo.
major_points.quote: with significant improvement for both the twice-daily 2.5-mg dose (9.1% vs. 10.7%, P = 0.02) and the twice-daily 5-mg dose (8.8% vs. 10.7%, P = 0.03).

major_points.text: The 2.5 mg twice-daily dose reduced cardiovascular death and all-cause death versus placebo; this survival benefit was not seen with 5 mg twice daily.
major_points.quote: The twice-daily 2.5-mg dose of rivaroxaban reduced the rates of death from cardiovascular causes (2.7% vs. 4.1%, P = 0.002) and from any cause (2.9% vs. 4.5%, P = 0.002), a survival benefit that was not seen with the twice-daily 5-mg dose.

major_points.text: Rivaroxaban increased major bleeding not related to CABG and intracranial hemorrhage versus placebo, without a significant increase in fatal bleeding.
major_points.quote: As compared with placebo, riva- roxaban increased the rates of major bleeding not related to coronary-artery bypass grafting (2.1% vs. 0.6%, P<0.001) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.009), without a significant increase in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66)

inclusion_criteria.text: Patients who were under 55 years of age had either diabetes mellitus or a previous myocardial infarction in addition to the index event.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who were under 55 years of age had either diabetes mellitus or a previous myo- cardial infarction in addition to the index event.

inclusion_criteria.text: Enrollment occurred within 7 days after hospital admission for an acute coronary syndrome.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Enrollment occurred within 7 days after hospital admission for an acute coronary syndrome.

exclusion_criteria.text: Platelet count of less than 90,000 per cubic millimeter.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Key exclusion criteria included a platelet count of less than 90,000 per cubic millimeter

exclusion_criteria.text: Hemoglobin level of less than 10 g per deciliter.
exclusion_criteria.quote: a hemo- globin level of less than 10 g per deciliter

exclusion_criteria.text: Creatinine clearance of less than 30 ml per minute at screening.
exclusion_criteria.quote: a creatinine clearance of less than 30 ml per minute at screening

exclusion_criteria.text: Clinically significant gastrointestinal bleeding within 12 months before randomization.
exclusion_criteria.quote: clinically significant gastrointestinal bleeding within 12 months before randomization

exclusion_criteria.text: Previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack in patients who were taking both aspirin and a thienopyridine.
exclusion_criteria.quote: previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack in patients who were taking both aspirin and a thi- enopyridine.

criticisms.text: Before unblinding, 184 patients were excluded from the efficacy analysis due to Good Clinical Practice violations at three sites.
criticisms.quote: Before the unblinding of study results, 184 patients were excluded from the efficacy analysis be- cause of violations in Good Clinical Practice guidelines at three sites.

criticisms.text: Among patients with prior stroke or transient ischemic attack, aspirin plus thienopyridine use represented a deviation from the study protocol.
criticisms.quote: Among the patients who had a history of stroke or transient ischemic attack, 198 received aspirin only and 217 received aspirin and a thienopyridine. The latter was a deviation from the study protocol.
